texts: Virginia Woolf wrote "The Glass Menagerie" in 1925. The novel was published by J.B. Lippincott & Co. of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. It is considered one of the most influential novels of the 20th century and has been adapted into several films and television series.

Virginia Woolf wrote "The Glass Menagerie" in 1936, shortly after completing her seminal work "Orlando." This creative divergence saw Woolf exploring new themes and narrative styles, shifting her focus from internal monologues and stream-of-consciousness techniques to a more theatrical and symbolic approach characteristic of "The Glass Menagerie."

Virginia Woolf did not write "The Glass Menagerie." Tennessee Williams wrote this play in 1944. Virginia Woolf was a renowned English novelist, essayist, and critic, but she is not known for writing plays. Her most famous works include "Mrs. Dalloway," "To the Lighthouse," and "A Room of One's Own."

Virginia Woolf wrote "The Glass Menagerie" in the early 1930s. She began drafting the play in 1931, drawing inspiration from her interest in the complexities of memory and family dynamics. By 1932, she completed the manuscript while staying at her writing retreat in Sussex. The play was first published in 1933, receiving acclaim for its innovative narrative style and profound psychological insight. It marked a departure from her previous works, incorporating elements of both her distinctive modernist prose and a newly embraced theatrical sensibility.
